messages.content: You coach a learner of German (their own language is Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China)) who is rewriting part of a real post before publishing it. Two people talk to them: a reader from the community, who speaks German and reacts like a real person in the thread, and a tutor, who speaks Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) and addresses the learner informally, as a friendly tutor would. The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China).

Where it will be posted: Reddit 帖子（德语，发在 r/Munich 版块）. Readers: 慕尼黑的本地网友，多为德语母语者，熟悉租房市场.
The writer's note about it, in their words: 发在 r/Munich 的德语帖子，想问大家怎么找合租房。
The post so far:
<<<
Hallo zusammen,

ich bin seit drei Monaten in München und ich suche eine WG für nächste Semester. Ich habe schon viele Nachrichten auf WG-Gesucht geschrieben, aber niemand hat mir geantwortet. Vielleicht liegt es daran, dass mein Deutsch nicht so gut ist, oder weil ich noch keine Schufa habe?

Habt ihr Tipps, wie man eine gute Nachricht an die Vermieter schreiben kann? Ich bin ruhig, ich koche gern und ich kann bis 450 Euro bezahlen. Vielen Dank im Voraus!
>>>
The spot: "Habt ihr Tipps, wie man eine gute Nachricht an die Vermieter schreiben kann?" in Habt ihr Tipps, wie man eine gute Nachricht an die Vermieter schreiben kann?
What is wrong there: 德语读者看到 Nachricht 加 gute，通常先理解为「好消息」，再看 schreiben 时才会改成「写一条好的消息」，两种读法在这里都说得通。读者需要先判断作者是在写询问信，还是有好消息要告诉房东，否则无法确定这句话在问什么。
What the writer means (confirmed by them): 想请教怎样写一条给房东的好询问消息
The learner will now write this part themselves in German. Prepare everything the session needs, in this order:
- reader: what the reader says on reaching this spot as it stands: one short line in German (at most 15 words), in character (puzzled, curious, teasing; never a teacher). The reader cannot read Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China): an untranslated passage is simply a gap to them, so react to what is missing and never mention the other language.
- replaces: exactly "Habt ihr Tipps, wie man eine gute Nachricht an die Vermieter schreiben kann?", copied character for character (the text around it is someone else's business). ref must fit in its place.
- keep: every point, detail, question, hedge and feeling in replaces, as short English notes, in order. The reference must carry each one unless the writer's meaning above drops it.
- ref: the reference version: what a fluent member of this community would write here to say exactly what the writer means, in the writer's voice and register. Keep everything the writer already says that still serves this meaning (their evidence, their reasoning, their own words) and add only what is missing. Never invent facts the writer has not given, here or in what they told you: no scene, event, line or detail from a work, no names, numbers, dates, quotes or personal circumstances. Where the meaning needs one (the evidence, which scene, what happened to them), write a short placeholder in its place, in German, between ⟨ and ⟩ (for example ⟨the scene you mean⟩), and the writer will fill it in. Where the problem is how the sentence is built (order, emphasis, angle, nominalisation), rebuild it the way this community would say it; do not stop at the smallest fix. Keep the strength the writer confirmed: where the problem is how something lands on its reader (too pushy, too blunt) and the writer means a firm need, a request or a demand, say it the way this place says such things politely and keep it firm; never turn it into something optional or a passing wish. Where the writer reached for an image or a joke, use this community's own equivalent if it has one rather than flattening it into plain words. Where the writer built a figure on purpose (a parallel or echo, a deliberate repetition, wordplay), ref keeps the figure and only puts natural words into it; the why note for such a word says the figure works and why the word changes. ref never says again what the post already says right before or after the replaced text (a reason or detail the next sentence gives stays there). ref replaces exactly the replaces text and carries every keep note and every name, title or label in it (a dish's name before its description, a person's name); it is the final text for that span: anything else wrong or unnatural inside it is fixed too, even where it is the writer's own wording. The writer's voice stays: casual spelling and capitalisation (all lowercase, capitals for emphasis, keysmashes, stretched letters, a missing apostrophe in a contraction), slang, emoji and the community's own shorthand, wherever fluent members of this community write that way too; so does a greeting or a word from another language used as flavour that readers will get. Names (characters, people, usernames, places, the community's terms) are the writer's: leave how they spell and capitalise them and which name they use, unless a reader could not tell who is meant. None of these is a problem in either pass. But wording carried over from Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) (a calque, a collocation, structure or set phrase a fluent writer would not produce) is not voice: it is a problem however casual the post. ref keeps that voice. Put [square brackets] around two to four single words that carry the key choices.
- alts: one or two other natural ways to say it, without brackets.
- pieces: three to eight hint pieces: the content words and short collocations (one to three words) that carry the meaning, including the writer's own words worth reusing. Each piece is German words only: no grammar notes, glosses, symbols or instructions. A piece names a word, never how to use it ("worth", not "worth + -ing" or "worth coming"). Not consecutive chunks of ref, no function-word glue, no full clauses: the learner must still build the sentence. "x / y" offers a fork.
- construct: the one reusable pattern this spot teaches, as a learner would jot it in a notebook: at most eight words, a German frame with one placeholder ("X left him + adjective", "What really got me was …"), optionally a short Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) gloss. Not a grammar formula.
- why: one entry per choice in ref that the learner might not make themselves. label: the German words; note, in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China): why this choice here, contrasted with what the learner wrote or would likely write, with a nuance or a tiny example when it helps. Concrete and specific, never "more natural" or "more appropriate" alone.
- checks: the mistakes this learner is likely to make on a first try, most important first: missing a part of the meaning, a structure carried over from Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China), the specific error already in their draft, a wrong word for this sense. For each: problem (what the grader should look for, in English); reader (optional: how the reader reacts when it happens, one German line in character, only when the meaning really suffers); hint (Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China): a nudge that points at the gap without giving the words); tell (Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China): says the fix plainly, with the words).
- success: the reader's reaction once the learner gets it right: in German, in character, at most 12 words, a reaction to what is now said (not a summary of it).
- prompt: the tutor's instruction in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) to start writing: one short sentence that fits the size of the spot (a clause, a sentence, a passage). The writer has just confirmed what they mean, so do not restate it; never mention punctuation, span boundaries or what comes after; never contain any word or structure from ref.

Wofür denn, du suchst doch noch eine WG?","replaces":"Habt ihr Tipps, wie man eine gute Nachricht an die Vermieter schreiben kann?","keep":["asking the group directly (ihr)","asking for tips","how one does it (general, not a personal case)","the message should be good","the message goes to the landlords (die Vermieter)","it is a question, not a statement","kann: can, as in knowing how to do it"],"ref":"Habt ihr Tipps, wie man eine gute [Anfrage] an die Vermieter [formuliert]?","alts":["Habt ihr Tipps, wie man eine gute Anfrage an die Vermieter schreibt?","Habt ihr Tipps, wie man den Vermietern eine gute Anfrage schickt?"],"pieces":["Anfrage","formulieren","Tipps","Vermieter","wie man"],"construct":"Habt ihr Tipps, wie man X formuliert? / 你们有没有怎么写X的建议？","why":[{"label":"Anfrage","note":"德语里 Nachricht 可以指任何消息，包括好消息，所以 gute Nachricht 容易被读成「好消息」。在租房帖里说 Anfrage，就是给房东的询问消息，读者一看就懂，这也是 WG-Gesucht 上的常用词。"},{"label":"formuliert","note":"schreiben 也说得通，但 eine Anfrage formulieren 是更地道的搭配，强调措辞和表达方式，正好对应你想问的「怎么写」。"}],"checks":[{"problem":"The word for the message must make clear it is an inquiry to landlords, not good news; Nachricht plus gute alone is ambiguous.","reader":"Gute Nachricht? Wofür denn, du hast doch noch gar keine Wohnung?","hint":"想想哪个词能让人一下子知道这是问房东的消息，而不是好消息。","tell":"把 Nachricht 换成 Anfrage，写成 eine gute Anfrage。"},{"problem":"A wrong word for the sense: Frage means a question, not a message to a landlord asking about a room.","reader":null,"hint":"你要的是给房东发的那种询问消息，不是一个问题本身。","tell":"用 Anfrage，不要用 Frage；Frage 只是「问题」。"},{"problem":"The question must still ask the group for tips on how to write it; a grader should not accept a version that asks what the landlords want or just states the problem.","reader":null,"hint":"句子要先问大家，再说你想知道的是怎么写。","tell":"保留 Habt ihr Tipps，后面接 wie man ... 说明要问的是写法。"}],"success":"Ach so, jetzt verstehe ich, was du willst. Dann her mit den Tipps!","prompt":"现在用德语把这句话写出来，语气像在论坛里随口问大家一样。"}
